decisive_items: chest pain consistently presented during physical activity
Patient developed left bundle-branch block (LBBB) in stage 2 at heart rate of 107 beats per minute with chest pain
Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities
response.rationale: Exertional angina with a normal coronary CTA and an exercise-induced LBBB that resolves with rest best fits Cardiac Syndrome X (angina with normal coronaries and abnormal exercise ECG); vasospasm typically occurs at rest, CAD is excluded by CTA, and structural/valvular causes lack supporting findings.

rejected.why: Vasospastic angina usually occurs at rest, whereas chest pain was consistently exertional; no ST elevation or rest pattern.
Coronary artery disease is effectively excluded by normal coronary CTA.
Mitral valve prolapse lacks characteristic murmur/click and does not explain exercise-induced LBBB with normal coronaries.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is less likely given normal baseline ECG and no murmur, syncope, or family history; CTA does not assess hypertrophy.
Aortic stenosis is unlikely without murmur or LVH and with normal baseline ECG; CTA does not assess valve.
